# 1.2.85 - every project change through one queue, projects and traps by the rules, and projects that open, breach, seal and mend

Two stages on this line, shipped as one train (E15 ships with E36): E36 in full - every change of a project goes through one
function, `applyProjectChange`, in one queue on the primary GM - and E15 in two parts - projects, traps, the overflow and
Monocubs by the rules (part 1), then Secret Passage, Breach the Wall and the owner's three projects of 15.10, Seal the passage,
Close the breach and Repair an item (part 2). Ten changes of one project asked at once land, each once, in their order; a
trap's bar taken back under its target disarms the trap and keeps the mark that it fired (the owner's D40); a target lowered to
or under a project's progress finishes it. An indirect murder's concealment bonus is paid on any outcome and kept by a Reroll,
a Loaded Die sets one of the two dice to 12 at random, and a Monocub starts clean. A finished Secret Passage gives its builder a
passage, a finished Breach the Wall cuts the real wall and forces the room beyond, and the three projects of 15.10 seal a
passage, give a breached wall back or mend an item. None of it has been tried at a real table yet (Known gaps); everything
measured below was measured in the test harness. CI's push run on 1cf6fd4 is red on one tier-2 test (Checked).

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **Every change of a project is made on the primary GM.** The Project Manager, the project window, the Countdowns tray, a
   Call, a Reroll, an Earthquake and a player's Work, Sabotage or share each hand their change to one queue there; another GM's
   change is sent to the primary and answered. When the primary leaves while another GM waits, that GM is told at once that no
   answer came; the wait's own clock is 30 s, a number chosen, not measured at a table. On a project's row in Daggerheart's
   Countdowns tray, - and + change the bar by one through that queue, Delete removes the project and its token, and Reveal and
   Hide are not offered; the tray was read in Daggerheart 2.10.5's source, not tried on v14.
3. **The project stores.** The GMs' project secrets now also hold a Secret Passage's or another preset's target, its stretch of
   wall and who found the project by Observe, and which roll's Reroll a finished project is kept for. A project token's record
   is written in the same queue. One new GM store, "The secret passages a project made this season", is kept in a setting
   nobody is shown, synced between the GMs and backed up, and cleared by the reset group now named "Who knows each secret
   passage, the passages projects made and their breaches (the GMs' passages stay, and whoever knew one at season start knows
   it again)". The season's projects are reset by the primary GM alone; another GM reads "Only the primary GM, {name}, can
   reset the season, so that one browser decides what every GM's copy of the case loses. Ask {name}, or reset when you are the
   only GM connected."
4. **The overflow's rules are trimmed once, on the primary GM's first load of 1.2.85** (the migration `trimOverflowRules`).
   Through 1.2.84 every Apply in Despair Flow saved the whole catalogue, so a default changed later never reached the world.
   Now the world keeps only what the GM changed - the threshold and each effect's on/off and size - read against 1.2.84's
   defaults, and everything else follows the module's defaults. No default number moves in 1.2.85, so a world sees the same
   overflow as before. A GM who saved a value equal to 1.2.84's default on purpose cannot be told from the old Apply: that value
   follows the default from now on.
5. **Walls a breach cuts and gives back.** A finished Breach the Wall is the only road on which the module makes a wall. The wall
   keeps its id and every field but its coordinates and becomes the piece before the stretch; the hole is a new wall that stops
   nothing; a copy is the piece after. Closing the breach - from the Passages tab, by a Close the breach project, by a Reroll
   that takes the breach back or at the season reset - writes the coordinates back and deletes the pieces, so the wall is as it
   was. If a GM deletes the original wall while its breach stands, a close gives the room beyond back and drops the breach, and
   the GM reads "the wall it was cut from is gone. The room beyond is given back; delete the hole by hand with the walls tool."
   The room beyond is marked forced on every piece of it, and the season reset takes that mark off every forced room of every
   scene.
6. **Passages a project grants** live in the new store, not in the GMs' map: the Passages tab shows them with the origin
   "Project" and the ways "built" and "shared", and the season reset takes them with their knowers. The reset window counts
   what it takes, as "{n} secret passages projects made", "{n} breaches, their walls made whole" and "{n} students who know a
   secret passage".
7. **Settings, keys and texts.** One new setting nobody is shown (the season's passages store); no new setting you see and no
   new keybinding. `lang/en.json` goes from 3774 strings to 3888 (114 added, 0 removed, 17 reworded) and `lang/pl.json` from
   4569 to 4693 (124 added, 0 removed, 18 reworded); the ten more in Polish are the new sound's two lines and the few/many
   forms of four counts. The five project kinds keep their English names in Polish.

## At the table

### For the GM

- **One queue for a project.** Ten +1 asked at once - the tray's +, a Hope Call, a player's Work and a GM's own - end at 10, each
  once, in their order. Each road writes once; a Save in the Project Manager over several rows writes once, and a row left as it
  was writes nothing. Two Sabotages at once make one repair. A share and a revoke asked together both land; a window's Save
  changes only the boxes the GM changed, applied to who sees the project then.
- **D40, the trap's bar.** A watched trap's bar taken back under its target disarms the trap and keeps the mark that it fired;
  filled again it arms unless it has fired, with one receipt per arming. A Reroll that fills a bar is announced once, one that
  takes it back is not announced and disarms its trap, and an Earthquake is one card.
- **A target lowered to or under the progress finishes the project**: one announcement, the trap and the thaw, as a filled bar.
- When part of what a finished project does could not be done, the GMs read "{name}: part of what finishing it (or taking it
  back under its target) does could not be done ({error}). The bar stands as it is; the console has the details." and the
  change stays made.
- **The token follows its project.** After each change one function puts the token right: moved once into a new room, tinted
  when finished, shown or hidden on each browser as soon as a share or a revoke lands, and kept off the map when a GM took it
  off by hand. A token dragged into another room is not moved back, and a second GM's project gets one token.
- **The project window.** A token dropped just inside a room's wall moves its project into that room. A proposal opens on its
  own scale, and an off-scale target is offered. An edit with Indirect murder names its killer or is refused with "An indirect
  murder needs a killer: pick who it is visible to, or approve it from the proposal card."; the viewer boxes of a public
  project open when Secret or Indirect murder is ticked. The trap's fields show only with Indirect murder, the viewers only
  with Secret or Indirect murder.
- **An Earthquake** now reads "The building shakes and work is undone: every project still under way loses {n} progress." and
  takes nothing from a finished or a frozen project.
- **A watched trap's receipt** says no "Awaiting a ruling." and plays no sound or popup; a plant trap's card keeps its Plant
  button and its question.
- **Despair Flow, the overflow.** Save writes only what differs from the defaults and nothing when nothing does; an emptied
  threshold field changes nothing and posts no card; an effect's size is held to 0-5. A darkening drawn during a Class Trial
  waits for the next time of day after the trial: its card reads "{n} points of spilled Despair have found a use. From the next
  time of day after the trial, for one time of day, this is what the school becomes:", Despair Flow reads "Right now: {count}
  of {max}. {what} was announced in the trial and waits for the next time of day.", a spill while it waits arms nothing, and
  the season reset clears it.
- **Despair Flow, the pools.** Save writes only the rows the GM changed or that were set before, and gives a student just ticked
  a Monokuma no row. A never-assigned student's pool is drawn as "{name} (fallback)", dim, beside every pool's plain name, so
  the first pool can be picked in one Save; the count of students kept out reads "Outside every pool", the pools' first column
  "Account", and Split evenly stands on the students' tab alone.
- **The Monocubs window** has short headers and the Silenced rule as its column's tooltip, and the Silenced box reads "Tick
  Monocub first" until the row's Monocub box is ticked.
- **A Monocub starts clean**: made from a student, it holds 0 Hope and no Health or Sanity marked, carries neither Wounded nor
  Breakdown, and has its two actions whatever its Health. A Confusion critical that moves nothing says so - "The player had
  every action left: there was none to give back." or "The player had no action left to waste." - and gives no free action.
- **A Loaded Die sets one of the two dice to 12 at random**, Hope or Fear, and the roll names which. A player's manual 2d12 feeds
  no pool; a Daggerheart duality roll still does.
- **Secret Passage and the other four kinds at the approval.** The window opens on the GMs' reading of where the builder stands
  and on the GMs' size, a repair's by the item's tier as the GMs hold it. For a Secret Passage, Secret is ticked and held - in
  the edit window and the manager too, so no road makes it public - and "Pick the stretch on the wall" picks it on the wall
  between the two rooms: Create is refused before a pick ("Pick the stretch of wall the secret passage goes through first."),
  another wall reads "Click on the wall between the project's two rooms.", and a stretch that is the whole wall is refused
  ("the stretch takes the whole wall, and nothing of it would stand. Pick a shorter stretch."). Seal the passage and Close the
  breach are approved only for a passage or a breach with a side in the builder's room; Repair an item only for an item on the
  builder's own sheet, carried or stashed, never a party actor's (the owner, 19.10). The primary judges each one again when it
  is finished.
- **When a finished project cannot do its part**, the GMs read why in the table's language, such as "{name} is finished, but its
  secret passage could not be opened: {why}", with one of 30 reasons or, for any other, "the module could not say why; the
  reason is in the GM's console." The approval window says the same reasons ("This cannot be done now: {why}").
- **The Passages tab** lists a breach as Kind "Breach" with Show and "Close the breach"; the GMs' Close the breach stays beside
  the players' project.
- **A forced room nobody owns** is told to the GMs alone: "A breach forces {room} open. Until the wall is repaired, its lock and
  its bedroom door stop nobody."
- **A Reroll takes each of the five back.** It removes a built passage and its knowers, gives a breached wall back and the room
  beyond, reopens a sealed passage, cuts a closed breach again (or tells the GMs "A Reroll took back {name}, but its breach
  could not be cut again: {why}") and breaks a repaired item again. A passage the hole showed is secret again after a Reroll's
  undo or the season reset. Each of the five is kept, finished, until the Reroll bookmark of the character whose roll finished
  it names another roll.

### For players

- **An indirect murder pays its concealment bonus on any outcome.** A lone Work that misses on a murder plan adds +1 progress,
  and its Reroll to 18 ends the bar at 3. The miss's card shows the +1 and counts as a success for a trap watching "Somebody
  works on a named project".
- **A Contribution** (a Hope Call) to an indirect murder rolls to hide its traces and leaves one, as a Work does; a Patronage
  (a Despair Call) on it rolls no cover. The trap's budget reads "A trap is built as projects. Budget about {low}-{high} progress
  across them, roughly four to six actions, or it costs more to set than it is worth.", its {low}-{high} read as 7-10.
- **A Loaded Die** reads "Loaded Die is armed. One of the two dice, at random, is set to 12 and the other is thrown - a very high
  total, and a critical only if that one comes up 12 as well."
- **Playing a Monocub**: you start with 0 Hope and no marks, keep two actions whatever your Health, and carry no Wounded or
  Breakdown. A Confusion critical that moves nothing tells its target "A moment's luck, but no action of yours was spent:
  nothing comes back." or "A moment's confusion, but you had no action left to lose.", one card, not two.
- **A Call is refused before its confirm**: a student under the Despair Call Silence is barred at once, and a second Loaded Die
  pressed is refused with no window. New Rule's confirm stays off until you write something.
- **What the explainers say.** "Every pool's count is public - the rows show how full each one is. Only the overflow's count is
  hidden from you."; with an empty hat, "Nothing is in the GM's hat right now, so the overflow will not fire until they put
  something in it."; "Players see “?” rather than the number: when it fires is Monokuma's to know. Nothing about the
  investigation lives in it."; and the actions: "Two each time of day. Searching a room, working on a project, observing a
  trace, analyzing a Truth Bullet - each of those is one. A Short Rest costs one, a Long Rest both." The silence badge reads
  "Sworn to silence", its tooltip "You stumbled onto the crime. You may not discuss it until this chapter ends; Confusion still
  works."
- **Propose a project has a Kind**: "A project of your own", or one of Secret Passage, Breach the Wall, Seal the passage, Close
  the breach and Repair an item where there is something to name. Secret Passage and Breach the Wall are offered beside a wall
  your room shares with another room on your floor, named as you know it under "Through the wall to". Each kind says what it
  is: "A secret passage through a wall of the room you are in: Hand, Complex (6), always secret. Only you, and whoever the
  project is shared with before it is finished, will know it."; "A breach through a wall of the room you are in: Body, Complex
  (6). Once it is finished the hole is there for everyone to see."; "Seal the passage: Hand, Complex (6). Once it is finished
  the passage is closed, for you and for everyone who knows it; a GM can open it again."; "Close the breach: Body, Complex (6).
  Once it is finished the wall stands whole again."; "Repair an item: Hand; Trivial (3) for an item of Tier 0 or 1, Complex (6)
  for Tier 2 or 3. Once it is finished the item is whole again." Seal the passage takes Hand and Close the breach Body, which
  the GM may change at the approval (the owner, 19.10).
- **A finished Secret Passage**: its builder reads "Your secret passage is finished: {from} - {to}. You can walk through it.", and
  each student of a player it was shared with before it was finished reads "A secret passage opens to you: {from} - {to}." - a
  share counts per player, so all of that player's students learn the passage; the students of its finders' and of the
  builder's own players are not counted as shared. Whoever found the project by Observe, and whoever such a finder let in,
  reads "The secret project you found is finished: {name}." and learns no passage.
- **A finished Breach the Wall** is told to the rooms. When the builder stands in one of the two rooms, the project's room reads
  "{name} breaks through a wall of this room: there is a breach in it now." and the room beyond "{name} breaks through a wall
  into this room from the other side: there is a breach in it now."; when the builder is elsewhere, unnamed, "A wall of this
  room gives way: there is a breach in it now." and "A wall of this room bursts open from the other side: there is a breach in
  it now."; "You hear a heavy crash beyond the wall, from {room}." in the rooms beside, nameless. A bedroom's owner reads "Somebody has broken through a wall into your bedroom, {room}. Until the wall is
  repaired, its door stops nobody." The room beyond is open to everyone - its GM's lock and its bedroom's key lifted until the
  wall is repaired, its seal lifted to the end of the time of day with no Despair given back (the bedroom owner's card, or the
  GMs', adds "The seal on it is broken until the end of this time of day."); a Chained student is still stopped, a seal set
  after the breach holds, and the trial's lock stands.
- **Seal the passage** closes a passage you know - one a GM drew too - for everyone who knows it; they keep knowing it, and a GM
  can open it again. **Close the breach** gives the wall back. **Repair an item** takes the broken mark and the wear off one
  usable or tool of your own and reads "{item} is whole again."

### For everybody

- **A breach is seen on every browser**: the hole stops nothing, the rest of the wall stands, and the breach's own sound
  (`wallBreached`) plays to the students in the two rooms and the rooms beside them. Through a breach or a built passage
  another's bedroom is passed with no key (the owner, 18.10).
- **A project's token** is shown or hidden on each browser as soon as who sees the project changes (each browser runs its
  visibility pass on the change; read in the code, not measured on a player's canvas).

## Known gaps

- **LIVE-E36-01** (item 299, not tried yet): two GMs change one project at once - GM2's Save in the Project Manager and the
  primary's + in the tray, then a player's Work - one order, one completion card; the primary reloading while GM2 waits; how
  long GM2's change takes on a real server.
- **LIVE-E36-02** (item 300, not tried yet): Daggerheart 2.10.5's tray on v14 in both themes - - and + on a project row once each,
  Delete with its token, no Reveal or Hide, a player's + changing nothing, the menu with the tray open before load and after a
  reload.
- **LIVE-E15-01** (item 301, not tried yet): an indirect murder from proposal to trigger at a real table, with a real token drag.
- **LIVE-E15-02** (item 302, not tried yet): Breach the Wall and the three repairs on the v14 sandbox - the cards by who stands
  where, a secret build with the builder elsewhere, a GM-locked and a sealed room, a second GM's Close, a real v14 wall's fields
  on the hole and the copy, the proposal and approval windows in both languages.
- **LIVE-E15-03** (item 303, not tried yet): Secret Passage on a real canvas from proposal to a real Reroll's undo, the pick
  clicked on the board and the gap drawn.
- **Defaults kept, not yet ruled by the owner**: a Contribution to an indirect murder rolls its cover on Hope Calls only, not
  Patronage; a lone miss on an indirect murder reads +1 progress and a success to a trap watching it; Secret Passage's share
  counts per player; a passage the hole showed stays public after a GM's or a project's Close the breach (secret again after a
  Reroll's undo or the reset); a Mastermind's player has no road to seal a passage known by the Mastermind's door alone; the
  GMs' Close the breach puts a lifted seal back within the same time of day, as the Reroll's undo does; a window's Save changes
  only the boxes the GM touched.
- A secret project's cards - the proposal, the Work's roll, the done cards and the passage cards - reach every browser as stubs
  naming who spoke and to whom they were whispered, as other secret cards do outside an incident; whether to veil them is the
  owner's.
- A finished project kept for a Reroll is let go when a GM's bookmark of a roll is written; if that bookmark was dropped, the
  project stays until the next one of any character. A project whose room no scene holds keeps its token where it stands.
- Another GM whose change landed just before the primary left is told no answer came (the late answer is on that GM's console);
  a step already past its check when the primary changes still writes on the old primary.
- A player's own proposal form still draws the trap's condition whatever Indirect murder says. The budget's "roughly four to six
  actions" stands beside 7-10, unmeasured. A critical Help on a target at its maximum still gives nothing, now saying so; Support
  with a target is asked by the GM after the Spend, as before.
- A darkening already running at the verdict is cleared, as before; only one not begun waits. A spill while one waits leaves the
  count above X, so the boundary after next may draw a second darkening (not driven). Two options in Despair Flow can name one
  pool, its fallback and its plain name; not painted headless.
- A Reroll of a loaded roll keeps the roll's mark of which die was loaded though its dice are thrown again. Which die
  Daggerheart throws first is read in its 2.10.5 source as copied in the harness, not on v14.
- One breach to a wall: a second on a wall a standing breach was cut from is refused until the first is closed. Two breaches
  forcing one room keep it forced until the last is closed (not driven). A forced room renamed whole while its breach stands is
  given back by its pieces, but the breach's record and the seal put back still read its old name. The season reset unforces
  every forced room of every scene.
- "You hear a heavy crash beyond the wall, from {room}." names the room as Listen does, "Unexplored room {n}" for one never
  visited. Who stands where is read once at the completion, and a dead student is told as a living one. A builder dead before
  the end still gets the passage, the seal or the repair.
- A completion refused because its target changed leaves the bar full and the project kept for the Reroll, with the GMs' card;
  nothing offers to name the target again. A Secret Passage whose stretch a GM drew a passage on meanwhile is refused that
  way. A share of a Secret Passage after it is finished gives no passage.
- A sealed passage is told to nobody but the GMs' log and the builder's done card; a breach closed by a project to nobody beyond
  the done card. A Mastermind as a seal's builder knows, for the seal, only a passage with a cell of its own or a public one.
- The GM may still change the size of one of the five kinds at the approval, and the change is not recorded. A stack of two is mended as one item.
  A repair taken back by a Reroll puts the item down rather than back in hand; a Close the breach taken back cuts the breach
  again under the original project, telling only the GMs when it cannot.
- The reset window's count of students who know a secret passage counts who knows one now, not who forgets one. The 31 codes
  (30 reasons and "unknown") serve the GMs' cards and windows; what Propose a project and the bridge tell a player when they refuse is not among
  them.
- Not driven by a test: a project moved to another scene, a reload before ready, a player's canvas hiding a token after a share,
  a receipt read on a second GM, a token dropped on a wall two rooms share, a Contribution on a second GM's approval, two
  no-target Calls held together, Despair Flow at 1366x768 and with an Assistant GM's pool, a second GM's merge and a backup's
  restore of the season's passages, a secret breach's build, Propose a project's pickers for Seal the passage, Close the breach
  and Repair an item, and those three through scenario 76's windows.
